decisions.what the ink shows: The ornamental capital has a broad outer curve, upper return, and inward horizontal arm. It is G-like despite differing from the plain graph Gs elsewhere on the sheet. The ink does not incontrovertibly decide S versus G, so no resolution is made from permutation-group expectations. The J index is clear. Blind-audit B05 also leaves the typographic alphabet open: a calligraphic G fits the rounded body and inward arm. This alternative is added without resolving the capital or changing the preferred reading.

Two opposing curved sides meet at the middle with a separate horizontal cross stroke. All four occurrences of the relative-curve variable have this same ornate crossed shape, supporting the fraktur alternative. The symbol is live, before the uncancelled une and the separately cancelled courbe.

notes: The marginal note records the anabelian condition on (g, nu=card J). The NB identifies the J-labelled moduli object with the modular scheme carrying the exclamation exponent after choosing an isomorphism from [1,nu] intersect Z to J. It states smoothness and finite type over Z, and carries this assertion to the graph-labelled objects and the concluding pair involving Gamma. This is a source summary, not an independent mathematical verification.

Section 4 begins the theory of Mumford and Deligne. It introduces a schematic multiplicity S, a proper relative scheme X and a closed subscheme underlined I, then begins the definition of a relative MD curve by flatness, finite presentation and a geometric-point condition that continues after this leaf.

The manuscript leaves une before the struck courbe and the replacement schéma. This agreement mismatch is not corrected. The two ornamental group capitals remain doubtful S/G despite the expected interpretation of the surrounding groups.

The independent audit reads the shorthand as barred m from its curved lower body and detached upper bar; it remains unexpanded. The first de/des keeps the independent tiny final remnant in an in-place doubt; the later de is clear. All seven M letters are plain, both exclamation marks are right exponents, and all four relative-curve X letters share the ornate crossed form read as fraktur.

H's editorial head-page note acknowledges 10, so no omission is charged there. The faint footer 21 is transcribed but its hand is unidentified. H's section wrapper is not itself treated as source ink or as an omission.

At first-reading commitment, root had inspected all fourteen saved crops and agreed the decisions, retaining the two S/G marks and des|de. The first reader also inspected all fourteen crops. The independent reading is recorded separately in the audit documentation.

Independent audit: the moduli letters retain plain M, with upright first stems, unlike the longer curved initial feet of the script M forms on scans019/021. Both exclamation marks remain upper-right exponents. The two ornamental group symbols remain uncertain and now explicitly include a calligraphic-G realization. The verbal shorthand is revised to barred m after comparison with scan029 B12; this changes the preferred source sign, not its expansion in the text. All four X forms have opposing curved sides plus a separate central cross stroke and retain fraktur X. Both une endings have visible low final e bodies. The final la/le is left uncertain. The split title underline, g descender, underlined I, literal tt and curled base symbols were checked individually. No independent smoothness or moduli-scheme proof was performed.
